data.hypothesis: Two earlier OpenMP candidates were valid at 0.07065 s and 0.07149 s versus the 0.39008 s serial baseline, but the small difference does not establish a performance cause. This contrasting experiment uses explicit contiguous per-worker ranges to test whether avoiding worksharing-loop overhead helps larger inputs; a serial path below 128 elements avoids starting a team for small inputs. Any speedup remains unmeasured.

memory_lessons.applicability: Use as a reference when comparing this manually partitioned OpenMP variant; the small mean-time difference between prior candidates may be measurement variation.
memory_lessons.claim: The earlier parallel candidate measured 0.0706517 s and the explicit-serial-branch variant measured 0.0714892 s; both were valid, versus the serial baseline at 0.3900794 s. These measurements do not establish why their times differ.
memory_lessons.next_experiment: Measure the manual contiguous partition candidate against the serial baseline and prior OpenMP candidate, including small sizes and the official workload.

data.notes: No commands were executed and this candidate has not been measured. For n >= 128, each actual OpenMP worker receives a disjoint contiguous range and writes each assigned output; its scratch array is private. The serial path preserves the original arithmetic. The controller should verify full overwrite/correctness and measure small cases and the official workload; observed baseline and prior-candidate timings are reported only as context.
transformations: Keep the baseline binomial arithmetic and its operation order unchanged in both serial and parallel paths.
Use an explicit serial fallback for counts below 128 or a one-thread budget.
For larger inputs, cap the requested team at min(positive threads, count), assign each worker a contiguous range based on the actual team size, and keep the per-element scratch array local.
